newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere favoured in Thomson sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Lagardere favoured in Thomson sell-off.

text.p: Lagardere's bold moves to forge alliances with European defence powerhouses should help it win a bidding war with Alcatel Alsthom for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF, analysts said on Wednesday.

They said the pan-European nature of Lagardere's offer showed the conglomerate, with businesses ranging from publishing to missiles, was serving notice it planned to take a leading role in the restructuring of Europe's defence industry.
Lagardere bolstered its offer on Wednesday by securing a wide-ranging accord with German defence giant DASA, and 300 million pounds ($490 million) in financing from British Aerospace.
It also signed, as did Alcatel, a memorandum of understanding on possible future cooperation with British electronics group General Electric Co Plc.
Analysts said another lift was Lagardere's announcement that it would help finance the deal by issuing a five billion franc ($860 million) convertible bond, repayable in cash and Thomson-CSF shares.
They estimate offers for Thomson-CSF could fall in a range from 185 to 220 francs per share, with one share analyst valuing Thomson-CSF at 23 billion francs.

The rapid fire announcements on Wednesday overshadowed Alcatel's joint offer with family-held Dassault Industries which held out the possibility of future cooperation with state-owned aerospace group Aerospatiale.

"Lagardere is erasing the criticism of its financing, which had always been held against it and is showing that it understands the European game of the future," said Antoine Nodet, analyst with Dupont Denant.
"Alcatel has not brought any new advantages to its offer," he added. "Dassault remains a French company. Rich, but French."
Lagardere and Alcatel -- in a joint bid with Dassault Industries -- each said earlier on Wednesday that they made formal offers to take over the government's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF.
The government has said it would choose one of the bidders by June 30, and no announcement is expected before the second round of a parliamentary election scheduled for June 1.
Analysts said both companies were healthy enough to take over and run Thomson-CSF, but that Lagardere's offer made more industrial sense.
"From an industrial point of view both offers are seductive," said a second share analyst. "I prefer Lagardere's bid because of its military orientation."

But analysts agreed Alcatel was still in the running. "Up until now, the market has given the edge to Lagardere but we must remember that Alcatel and Dassault are planning to link up with Aerospatiale, which could make a difference," Nodet said.

The government has said it will merge Dassault and Aerospatiale this year and promptly privatise the newly-formed company, which would give Aerospatiale a role to play if Alcatel/Dassault wins the bidding war.
Investors, who sold Lagardere after the initial offer was made, took the company's shares off their lows after the announcement of its link with DASA and financing with BAe.
After falling by as much as 3.17 percent to 174.30 francs, Lagardere closed at 176 francs, off 2.22 percent.
Alcatel closed 0.92 percent off at 647 francs.
Worry about the convertible bond issue, which caused the initial sell-off of Lagardere, was overwhelmed by approval of the European nature of its offer, Nodet said.
Shares in Thomson-CSF closed 1.21 percent higher at 184.60 francs as investors bet the offer price would certainly be higher than 180 francs.
-- Paris Newsroom +331 4221 5452 ($ = 0.611 British Pounds) ($ = 5.817 French Francs)
